div.head: II Cn 48.1
div.ab: Gif he man gewundige, gebete þæt ⁊ gylde fulwite þam hlaforde, ⁊ æt bisceope þa handa alyse oððe hig alæte.
Gyf he man wundige, gebete þæt ⁊ gylde fulwite ðam hlaforde, ⁊ æt ðam bisceope þa handa alyse oððon híg forlete.
Gif he man gewundige, gebete þæt ⁊ gilde fullwite þam hlaforde, ⁊ æt biscope þa hande alysa oððe hig alæte.
Si aliquem uulneret, hoc emendet, et reddat plenam witam domino, et ab episcopo manum suam redimat uel amittat eam.
Quodsi ibi aliquem uulnerauerit, id illi emendet cui uulnus fecit, et domino illius plenam forisfacturam, et manum suam ab episcopo redimat aut perdat.
[48, 1] Qui si ibi hominem uulneret, emendet illud, et soluat plenam forisfacturam domino, et [ab] episcopo manus redimat aut illas amittat.
Gyf he man wundige, gebete þæt ⁊ gylde fulwite ðam hlaforde ⁊ æt ðam bisceope þa handa alyse oððon híg forlete.
Gif he man gewundige, gebete þæt and gylde fulwite þam hlaforde, and æt bisceope þa handa alyse oððe hig alæte.
Wenn er jemanden verwundet, büsse er das [dem Verletzten] und zahle Vollstrafe dem [Immunitäts]herrn, und löse vom Bischof die Hände oder verliere sie.
If he wounds someone, let him make amends for it [to the injured man] and pay the full fine to the [immunity-]lord, and redeem his hands from the bishop or lose them.
If he wounds anyone, he shall make amends for doing so, and shall pay the full fine to the lord and redeem his hands from the bishop or lose them.
If he wounds a man, he is to pay compensation for it and pay full fine to the lord, and redeem his hands from the bishop or forfeit them.
If he wounds anyone, he must pay compensation for that and pay the full penalty to the lord, and ransom his hands from the bishop or lose them.

note.seg: Cn meint, wie o. 30, 3b, den Empfänger des Strafgeldes für das vom Missetäter Verwirkte. Dieser war damals bereits oder wurde noch im 11. Jh. identisch mit dem Herrn der Gerichtsbarkeit; s. d. Gl 3. Ihn, und vielleicht auch den im 12. Jh. zumeist mit ihm identischen Vassallitätsherrn, meinen die wörtlich übersetzenden Q C. Dagegen ‘den Herrn des Verletzten’ versteht Inst: irrig, denn solche Busse hiesse ‘Schutz(bruch)’, nicht Strafe; auch war des Kirchengeld-Eintreibers Herr wohl regelmässig der—hier doch von ihm getrennt genannte—Bischof

Cn means, as above 30, 3b, the recipient of the fine for what the wrongdoer has forfeited. He was at that time already, or became in the course of the 11th cent., identical with the lord of the jurisdiction; see that word in Gl 3. It is he, and perhaps also the lord of vassalage, who in the 12th cent. was mostly identical with him, that Q C, translating literally, mean. Inst, on the other hand, understands ‘the lord of the injured party’: wrongly, for such a compensation would be called ‘(breach of) protection’, not fine; besides, the lord of the collector of church dues was probably as a rule the bishop — who is, after all, named separately from him here

EGu fordert hier ganzes Wergeld. Da eine Hand nur gleich ¹/₂ Wergeld gilt, meint Cnut, wie C und o. 30, 4, beide. Mercisch kommt handa für manum vor; Sievers Gram. 274 A 2: daher vielleicht der Irrtum in Q Inst.—Hier steht neben Leibesstrafe Strafgeld; Schreuer (Verbrechenskonk. 266) erklärt das durchs doppelte Delikt: Verwundung und Kirchengeldweigerung. Wohl war dadurch der Frieden sowohl des Staats wie der Kirche gebrochen. Allein jene Leibesstrafe ist nur noch Name für Geldstrafe, laut 48, 2 nicht mehr friedlos machend

EGu here demands the whole wergild. Since one hand counts as only ¹/₂ wergild, Cnut, like C and above 30, 4, means both. In Mercian handa occurs for manum; Sievers Gram. 274 A 2: hence perhaps the error in Q Inst.—Here a fine stands alongside corporal punishment; Schreuer (Verbrechenskonk. 266) explains this by the double offence: wounding and refusal of church dues. Probably the peace of both the state and the Church was thereby broken. But that corporal punishment is by now merely a name for a money penalty, no longer entailing outlawry, according to 48, 2

forlætan: ‘to loose’ Sweet; auch Mittelenglisch; Mätzner Wb 176 n. 5. Die Bed. fehlt Toller
forlætan: ‘to loose’ Sweet; also Middle English; Mätzner Wb 176 n. 5. The meaning is missing in Toller
Taken as sing. by Q and Inst., plural by Cons. In E. and G. the fine is the man’s wergeld, and as one hand is equal in value to half the wergeld Liebermann concludes that both are meant here.
